intro_html: This is the good part of Thanksgiving without the four days of preparation or the relatives. Turkey and peas in a poultry-seasoned gravy, stuffing baked golden across the top, all of it in one pan on a random Tuesday. Each serving lands at 575 calories with 39 grams of protein for about $1.84. Boxed stuffing mix is one of the cheapest carbohydrates in the store, and it never once pretended otherwise.
cost_closing_html: About $1.84 a serving for a plate that tastes like a holiday. The stuffing mix and the frozen peas are doing the budget work while the turkey does the protein work.
shop_smart: Stuffing mix goes on deep discount every November and keeps in the box for a year or more. Buy a stack then and you are cooking this dish at a fraction of the price all spring.
A frozen turkey breast roast is the cheapest way into this recipe outside the holidays. Roast one on a Sunday, dice it, and you have the protein for two batches.
Greek yogurt is standing in for sour cream in the gravy and costs less per ounce in the 32 oz tub. It also drops the fat without hurting the texture.
Frozen peas over canned, always. The store-brand 12 oz bags are the cheapest vegetable in this recipe and they hold their shape through the bake.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat, sprinkle in the flour, and whisk for two minutes until it smells nutty instead of raw.
Pour in the chicken broth and the milk slowly, whisking the whole time, and cook until the gravy thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Season the gravy with the onion powder, garlic powder, poultry seasoning, salt, black pepper, and a few dashes of hot sauce, then take it off the heat.
Stir in the Greek yogurt and the shredded cheddar off the heat so the yogurt does not break, then fold in the diced turkey breast and the frozen peas.
Spread the filling into a greased 9x13 pan and level it out.
Prepare the stuffing mix per the box directions but hold back a little of the liquid, then spoon it over the filling in an even layer and press it down lightly.
Bake at 375F for 30 to 35 minutes, uncovered, until the stuffing is browned on top and the gravy bubbles at the edges. Rest 10 minutes before portioning.
portion_html: Set the pan on the scale, subtract the empty pan weight, and divide by 14. Weigh each square into its container instead of guessing, since the stuffing layer makes the portions look bigger than they are. Every serving comes to 575 calories and 39 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Thanksgiving dinner on a weeknight budget, about $1.84 a serving. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, for $1 a month.

steps: Whisk flour into melted butter and olive oil for two minutes, then add the broth and milk and cook until thickened.
Season the gravy with onion powder, garlic powder, poultry seasoning, salt, pepper, and hot sauce, then remove from the heat.
Stir in the Greek yogurt and cheddar, then fold in the diced turkey and frozen peas.
Spread into a greased 9x13 pan and top with stuffing prepared per the box, pressed level.
Bake uncovered at 375F for 30 to 35 minutes until browned, rest 10 minutes, and portion into 14 containers.
